title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). For operational use the generated configurations must satisfy deterministic invariants—reachability, policy compliance, ordering and workflow constraints, and group-level safety—before any deployment. Prior work demonstrates prototypes for intent→configuration synthesis and advocates verifier/validator stages, but artifact-grounded empirical evidence quantifying generator→verifier→repair pipelines in a tightly controlled design is limited [1],[2],[3].

This study tests the preregistered question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? The design intentionally isolates the marginal repair effect on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only estimand) and therefore does not measure effects that would require independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, or mult-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and one hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 automated repair (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused diagnostic of the single repaired pair with archived validator traces. (5) Reproducibility guidance and bounded operational implications grounded in the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Recent NetOps and AIOps literature reports intent-driven configuration synthesis systems and prototype generator–validator pipelines with curated evaluation suites [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain research on generate→validate→repair (program repair, synthesis) shows verifier-assisted repair can improve correctness when the oracle is well-specified [4],[5],[6]. Surveys on agentic AI and LLM safety document hallucination and adversarial failure modes and recommend verifier gates and provenance for operational pipelines [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap positioning. Many prior demonstrations either evaluate first-pass generation accuracy across independent samples or present repair loops in software-engineering domains; few provide a preregistered paired design that reuses the identical initial candidate to isolate a repair-only effect. The supplied literature therefore motivates but does not answer whether a bounded verifier-triggered repair can recover invariant compliance from an identical initial candidate in NetOps—our experiment addresses that narrower empirical gap with archived artifacts and deterministic reconciliation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). Generation semantics were fixed to shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded episodes). The protocol allowed at most one automated repair call per task and specified a single confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The full preregistration and plan are archived and indexed by the execution manifest (preregistration SHA-256: bdfa0f64...).

Task generation and selection. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and selected deterministically per the preregistered cycle/offset mapping. The task bank targets very_hard and extreme workflow patterns with multi-device ordering constraints, dependency rules, group invariants, and an explicit required_sequence per task. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies; manifests are available in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Inclusion/exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks, syntactic pre-checks) were applied before model calls; the archived run recorded no preregistered exclusions.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared execution model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). That file records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset in the archived configuration is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; hosted-model nondeterminism therefore cannot be excluded. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider-call accounting in deterministic_reconciliation shows model_calls_used = 201 with stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Deterministic verifier and scoring rule. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acted as the oracle. The verifier deterministically parses generated commands, enforces allowed-field constraints, checks required_sequence ordering constraints, enforces group-level invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and flags violation codes. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 if and only if all required invariants pass. Per-episode validator traces (validation_before, validation_after) and violation codes are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Paired-experiment semantics and failed-call handling. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline and guarded episodes for a pair begin from the identical initial candidate; therefore, any observed difference in per-pair acceptance can only arise from the permitted verifier-triggered repair (a repair-only effect). The preregistered missingness plan treated persistent unparsable outputs as failures in sensitivity analyses; the archived run recorded no persistent unparsables and no missing pairs.

Statistical analysis plan and exact McNemar calculation. The primary confirmatory test was the exact two-sided McNemar applied to discordant counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). The executor computed the two-sided p by using the binomial distribution on n = n10 + n01 under H0: p = 0.5 with formula p_two = 2 * min{BinomialCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomialCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)} where k = n10. For our observed discordants (n = 1 with k = 1) the calculation is: BinomialCDF(1;1,0.5) = 1.0 and 1 − BinomialCDF(0;1,0.5) = 0.5, so p_two = 2 * min{1.0, 0.5} = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the risk difference used 10,000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729 (parameters recorded in analysis_log.jsonl). All analysis artifacts are archived in analysis/ (analysis/results.json, analysis/*.csv).

Reproducibility practice. The run archived: (a) per-call provider traces (execution/provider_calls/...), (b) shared-initial and condition-specific responses (execution/responses/...), (c) per-episode scoring records (execution/scoring/...), (d) task manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), (e) model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), (f) execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json, and (g) analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Reanalysis is reproducible by running paired_binary_analysis_v1 on execution/raw_results.jsonl with the archived analysis configuration.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting; provider-call audit stage counts are shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded numbers). The analysis/condition_summary.csv artifact reports: baseline successes = 199, failures = 1 (success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 (exact-binomial calculation shown in Methods). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]; these numeric results are verbatim from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and analysis/*.csv).

Repair activity and representative diagnostics. The guarded pipeline invoked one automated repair (stage count = 1). The repaired pair's validator_trace identifies the failure as a multi-step ordering/workflow violation against the task's required_sequence (the task manifest contains required_sequence and workflow_policies). The repair applied a small reordering patch to the command sequence so that the required_sequence ordering was satisfied; after repair the verifier returned valid = true. Representative artifacts for the repaired task (e.g., execution/responses/task-000008-*, execution/scoring/task-000008-*.json) and validator traces contain parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and violation_codes before and after repair. In the archived sample the repaired baseline occurred on a task with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3 (an extreme composite difficulty), consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering and dependency interactions concentrate failure risk.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination monitoring. The run recorded no excluded preregistered tasks and no missing pairs: complete_pairs = 200, baseline_only_observed_pairs = 0, guarded_only_observed_pairs = 0, both_missing_pairs = 0. analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged contamination entries. Provider-call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts indicating 200 shared initial generations and a single repair.

Exploratory descriptive diagnostics. The archived task manifests permit exploratory breakdowns by difficulty level (very_hard vs extreme), required_command_count, and changed_interface_count. Within the archived artifacts the lone baseline failure concentrated in an extreme/very_hard composite task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3), while the remaining successful tasks span required_command_count values from small to large. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg visualizes the per-condition rates and bootstrap distribution used for CI construction and is included in the artifact bundle.
sections.discussion:
Meaning of the estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because baseline and guarded conditions began from the identical initial candidate for every task, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair (a repair-only effect). This estimand does not capture benefits that could arise from alternative guarded designs such as independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature tuning, or multi-sample selection; separate preregistered contrasts are needed to estimate those interventions.

Statistical power and discrete inference regime. The preregistration targeted detecting ≈10–15 percentage-point paired improvements with N = 200 under baseline assumptions ~45–65% success. The observed baseline success (199/200 = 99.5%) far exceeded those assumptions, producing low realized power to detect small absolute differences and placing inference in a discrete regime of few discordants. In such regimes exact McNemar p-values can be uninformative for very small discordant counts (here p = 1.0 for a single discordant), so reporting paired-bootstrap CIs is important for bounding plausible effect sizes; our bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies that uncertainty.

Operational implications and scope. The archived evidence shows a single automated repair corrected a localized multi-device ordering fault in one extreme task. This supports the narrow conclusion that verifier-guarded repair can correct certain localized ordering faults on identical initial candidates in a deterministic synthetic setting. It does not imply that guarded repair will fix semantic misinterpretations of intent, omissions only observable in live dataplane telemetry, or outputs induced by adversarial poisoning. Live-device emulation, multi-model tests, or adversarial contamination experiments are necessary before operational claims can be extended.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and one initial generation per task restrict conclusions to repair effects only. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces encoded invariants but does not emulate live dataplane behavior or runtime telemetry; some risks require live execution testing. External validity: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: the small number of discordant pairs implies substantial uncertainty for small absolute effects; paired-bootstrap CI quantifies that uncertainty.

Reproducibility and archival guidance. All runtime parameters (declared_model/requested_model, maximum_attempts_per_call), per-call provider traces, shared-initial responses, condition-specific responses, per-episode scoring records, task manifests, model_configuration.json (temperature = null/unset), execution manifest, deterministic_reconciliation.json, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle. To reproduce the primary analysis: (1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl, (2) run paired_binary_analysis_v1 with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and resamples = 10000, and (3) verify analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv match the reported numbers. The execution manifest contains authoritative counts (model_calls_used = 201, stage_counts: 200 shared initial + 1 repair).

Recommended next steps grounded in the archived evidence. Future preregistered studies should (1) adopt independent first-pass guarded generation semantics to estimate guarded-prompt or constrained-prompt effects, (2) include multiple models to assess cross-model generality beyond gpt-5-mini, (3) expand task diversity and include live-device telemetry or deterministic dataplane emulation, and (4) include adversarial/contamination experiments. Each recommendation follows directly from limitations observed in the archived run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with a paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair. Artifact-grounded evidence supports the constrained conclusion that verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting. Broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
